evidence.note: Self-built engine tests during build: formula smoke tests, dependency/cycle/spill/aggregate checks, plus instrumented debugging of cycle detection and iterative calc on clear — verification steering fixes.
Ran full dev smoke suite, pulled failure details, applied targeted fixes across evaluator/server/tokenizer/operations, then re-ran to confirm — failure-driven loop, not just a green-run-and-done.
Created explicit verification tasks and ran performance benchmarks against the stated ceilings (1000-cell chain, 100k import), i.e. probing the performance bounds directly.
Persistence-across-restart probe surfaced a deserialize bug that was diagnosed and fixed — verification uncovering a real defect.
XLSX round-trip verified via openpyxl re-import and conditional-format style preservation, driving ~15 iterative xlsx.py edits until fidelity held.
Broad subsystem probes: collab backfill/dependents, goal-seek convergence + no-dependency rejection, iterative toggle, Excel edge cases (SUMIF/COUNTIF fixes), cross-sheet/locale/validation variants.

reasoning: The agent built targeted checks well beyond the smoke suite across nearly every subsystem — formula oracles, error-sentinel edge cases, spill, xlsx openpyxl round-trip, collab, goal-seek, iterative calc, locale, persistence — and benchmarked the stated performance ceilings, consistently using failures to drive fixes; this meets and exceeds the breadth of anchor 8. It falls short of 10 because the checks are disposable inline probes rather than a persistent systematic harness, and expected values appear largely hand-asserted rather than systematically grounded in the LibreOffice oracle corpus.
